hero.h1: EV charger in a garage and fire: is it safe to charge an electric car in a garage
hero.lead: Yes, if the charger is installed professionally. Data from insurers and the ADAC auto club do not show that electric cars burn more often than cars with a combustion engine. The bigger risk is an old socket and a circuit that runs under load for hours.

card.title: EV charger in a garage and fire
card.text: Do electric cars burn more often, where the real risk is and what the 2024 garage rulebook says.

blocks.p: Fear of fire is the most common question when someone in a building proposes a charger. The answer has two parts: what the data on cars say and what the installation in the garage has to meet.

p: Below are the insurer and fire brigade data, the rules of Serbia's garage rulebook and the questions neighbors ask. To see whether your spot meets the basic conditions for a charger, go to

blocks.p: The German Insurance Association (GDV) says its statistics show no sign that electric cars burn more often than cars with a combustion engine. ADAC takes the same view: there is no indication that electric cars, with or without a crash, are more prone to fire.
Cars burn regardless of drive type. According to GDV data, a total of 14,200 comprehensively insured passenger cars of all drive types burned in Germany in 2023.

Fire brigades take a similar view of underground garages. The association of heads of professional fire brigades in German cities, the German Fire Brigade Association and ADAC see no increased danger from electric cars parked in an underground garage. ADAC adds a condition: the wiring of the charging point must be professionally installed and maintained.

blocks.h2: How an electric car fire is different

blocks.p: The difference is in extinguishing, not in how often a fire starts. A battery fire is harder to put out: the battery has to be cooled for longer, which takes considerably more water.

The Swiss institute Empa tested an electric car fire in a tunnel and an underground garage. According to ADAC, the danger was not greater than with a petrol or diesel car. After a fire, however, the toxic residues have to be cleaned up professionally and the extinguishing water disposed of properly.

In a closed garage, it makes little difference to smoke and heat whether an electric or a conventional car is burning. That is why a garage's safety depends above all on its layout: escape routes, smoke extraction and the equipment for fire detection and extinguishing.

blocks.h2: The real risk: a socket and a circuit under long load

blocks.p: A car does not draw power like a hair dryer or a vacuum cleaner. It charges for hours without a break, and an ordinary socket and an old circuit are often not built for that kind of load.
ADAC does not recommend charging from a household socket for safety reasons alone. In its August 2026 study, it advises having an electrician check the home wiring beforehand if you have doubts.

p: Regular charging in a garage needs a dedicated circuit from the distribution board to your spot, with its own breaker and residual current device. When an ordinary socket is still an acceptable backup is explained in the guide

p.a: charging your car from a Schuko socket

blocks.p: At the end of that circuit goes a heavy-duty socket built for long charging or a wallbox. A licensed electrician decides the cable size, the protection and the route, and only they work in the distribution board.

There is a separate European document for charging circuits, HD 60364-7-722. It covers circuits that supply electric vehicles and circuits that take power from vehicles. When the work is done, ask the installer for a written report on testing the installation and keep it for the building manager.

Serbia applies the Rulebook on technical standards for fire safety of garages (Official Gazette of RS 31/2024 and 59/2025). It was first published on April 11, 2024, and replaced the rulebook from 2005.

The rulebook covers fire safety in the construction, extension and reconstruction of garages (Article 1). Article 3 states explicitly that a garage may include a space for charging electric vehicles. So charging in a garage is not prohibited.

Article 4 covers existing garages. In a reconstruction or extension, the rulebook applies only to the part of the building and the installations that the work concerns. That work must not reduce the fire safety of the existing building.

In medium and large underground garages and in large enclosed above-ground garages, the wiring and electrical equipment must meet the conditions for external influence class BD2 (Article 49). Other regulations and Serbian fire protection standards also apply to equipment and installations (Article 2).

The rulebook does not say whether installing one charger in an existing garage counts as a reconstruction. Ask a lawyer or a licensed fire protection designer, together with the question of which category your garage falls into.

blocks.h2: What the building manager and neighbors will ask

blocks.p: The residents' assembly decides on placing things on the common parts of the building and on the fee for them (Article 42, paragraph 1, item 16 of the Law on Housing and Building Maintenance). Decisions are generally taken by a simple majority of those present, while disposing of common parts takes 2/3 of all votes (Article 44). Ask a lawyer which majority applies to a charger in your building.
Answer fire questions with facts. Before the meeting, prepare answers to these questions:

ul: Who does the work, and is the electrician licensed?
Does the charger get a dedicated circuit with its own protection?
What conformity documents does the equipment have?
Who provides the written test report after installation?
How is consumption measured, and who pays for the power?
Can the building's connection handle the extra load?
